text:
sarah_sales: Quick presales question — FinHealth wants a 2-week POC. Requirements: tenant locked to Europe-only, 50ms p95 token latency target for chat endpoints, and a subprocessors roster for the regions. Also need confirmation on KMS/BYO availability and an estimated cost uplift for pinning. Can Dedicated or Hosted meet this, and what are ops handoff steps? cc @dinesh_eng @maya_ops

 dinesh_eng: Short answer: We can support with Dedicated or Private. Hosted can do region affinity but not strict tenant pinning (there's best-effort routing only). For strict residency you need Dedicated (tenant anchoring) or Private.

 maya_ops: EU regions we can offer: ireland (eu-west-1), frankfurt (eu-central-1), netherlands (europe-west3). Typical subprocessors in EU flows: AWS (Dublin, Frankfurt), GCP (Netherlands), Cloudflare (CDN), Fastly (edge), Sentry (errors). KMS: BYOK supported on Dedicated/Private. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default but we can do hosted-BYOK under an addendum. Link to subproc list: https://redwood.help/subprocessors (procurement pack).

 sarah_sales: Can you paste a short subproc bullet list I can give procurement + the hosted vs dedicated KMS line? They want to include it in their security questionnaire today.

 dinesh_eng: Short list: - AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1) - GCP (europe-west3) - Cloudflare - Fastly - Sentry - HashiCorp Vault (partner KMS) Hosted vs Dedicated KMS: Hosted = Redwood-managed KMS (keys stored within EU regions on request, default MSA), Dedicated/Private = customer BYOK possible (HSM-backed exchange).

 maya_ops: Pricing note: strict tenant pinning implies reserving capacity -> typical uplift is a flat reservation fee + ~15-25% per-token cost delta depending on instance mix. Exact number needs model + qps. I can do a rough estimate if you share expected rps and seq len.

 security_bot: Confirming attestation requirements: current EU-only attestation pack includes DPA, SOC2 summary, subprocessors list PDF, and dataflow diagram. BYOK requires an MSA addendum and completed KMS exchange checklist.

 sarah_sales: They also want failover behavior documented — prefer primary: ireland, failover: frankfurt only. Is that straightforward?

 dinesh_eng: Yes — we support region-preference with a strict fallback ordering in Dedicated. Behavior: primary routes all requests to ireland; if capacity/health breaches threshold, requests failover to Frankfurt. Note: cross-region failover will change latency and may trigger egress billing depending on contract. For VPC/private deployments we can avoid public egress.

 dinesh_eng: Example routing policy (config snippet):

 ```json
 {
   "tenant": "finhealth-poc",
   "routing": {
     "mode": "strict_pin",
     "primary_region": "eu-west-1",
     "failover_order": ["eu-central-1"]
   },
   "kms": {
     "mode": "byok_optional",
     "requirements": "if_byok -> key_exchange_workflow"
   }
 }
 ```

 dinesh_eng: Ops lead time: Dedicated tenant provisioning 5-7 business days after contract and capacity allocation. BYOK adds ~3-5 business days for key setup and attestation. Need: customer CIDR (if VPC peering), desired failover order, and whether BYOK is mandatory.

 maya_ops: I'll start a handoff ticket and upload the EU attestation pack + rough pricing band. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/POC-1234 — adding presales checklist and subproc pdf.

 sarah_sales: Perfect. Can you also drop a tiny latency test script I can share with the customer so they can validate p95 from their side?

 dinesh_eng: Yep — lightweight example (curl + jq):

 ```bash
 for i in {1..100}; do
   start=$(date +%s%3N);
   curl -s -X POST https://eu.api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -d '{"input":"ping"}' >/dev/null;
   now=$(date +%s%3N); echo $((now-start));
 done | jq -s 'sort | {p95: .[94]}'
 ```

 maya_ops: I'll own the ops handoff once you confirm BYOK and CIDR. @sarah_sales please collect those from the customer and update the ticket.

 sarah_sales: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
